subject: Engineering Fundamentals
title: Wind Load: Invisible Force, Visible Damage
description: A short lesson to help you apply Wind Load: Invisible Force, Visible Damage.

hook.text: The Burj Khalifa sways up to 2 meters at the top in high winds. It was designed to do that.

buildup.text: Wind load increases with height squared. A building twice as tall faces four times the wind pressure.

discovery.text: Wind doesn't just push. It creates vortexes on the leeward side that suck the building backward rhythmically.

twist.text: Vortex shedding can match a building's natural frequency, causing resonance — the same effect that toppled Tacoma Narrows.

climax.text: The Burj Khalifa's Y-shape disrupts vortexes. Each setback breaks the wind pattern at a different height.

punchline.text: Shape the building to confuse the wind. Problem solved.

quiz.question: Why is the Burj Khalifa shaped like a Y?
options: It maximizes floor space on each level for more occupants
The shape disrupts wind vortexes at different heights
It allows three separate elevator systems to operate independently
